
```{r, include= FALSE}
#dependent variable 
netMLC <- sienaDependent(array(data = c(wave1, wave2), dim = c(dim(wave1), 2)))
#behavioural variable
behy <- df2 %>% 
  dplyr::select("socsatw1n", "socsatw2n") %>%
  as.matrix()
behMLC <- sienaDependent(behy, type = c("behavior"))
#independent variables
parent_edu_ccv <- coCovar(as.numeric(df2$parentshighf))
gender_ccv <- coCovar(as.numeric(df2$genderf))
ethnicity_ccv <- coCovar(as.numeric(df2$ethnicityf))
#data
mydata <- sienaDataCreate(netMLC, behMLC, parent_edu_ccv, gender_ccv, ethnicity_ccv)
#effects structure
myeff <- getEffects(mydata)
effectsDocumentation()
#?
myAlgorithm <- (sienaAlgorithmCreate(projname = "results"))
```

## Model 0: Simple Model

```{r,include= FALSE}
simple_model <- readRDS("simple_model.rds")
results_m0 <- data.frame(
  effect = simple_model$effects$effectName,
  b = simple_model$theta,
  se = simple_model$se,
  t = simple_model$theta / simple_model$se,
  p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(simple_model$theta / simple_model$se))
)
```

The null model converges at 0.13, which is acceptable. The outcomes of the simple model (Table 1)
show things we have already learned from the descriptive results and the network graph, namely that
there is a significantly bigger chance that one does not observe a tie, compared to the chance that
one would observe a tie, thus meaning that density is very low (*b* = -2.67, *SE* = 0.53, *p*
\>.01). The reciprocity statistic is positive, indicating that the students in the network do tend
to reciprocate their tie (*b* = 2.09, *SE* = 0.14, *p* \>.01)

Change in social satisfaction is not significant on a linear level (*b* = 0.17, *SE* = 0.14, *p* =
0.22), but it is significant on a quadratic level (*b* = -0.34, *SE* = 0.15, *p =* 0.02) and going
into a negative direction, which indicates that students whose social satisfaction is below the mean
have a stronger tendency to move towards to mean than students who are above the mean.

However, these statistics on their own do not mean a lot yet, as the statistics as defined in the
methodology need to be added to the models and some additional control statistics.

**Table 1:** *Results of Model 0*

```{r}
pander::pander(results_m0)
```

## Model 1: Homogeneity in Reciprocated Ties

```{r, include= FALSE}
model1 <- readRDS("model1.rds")
results_m1 <- data.frame(
  effect = model1$effects$effectName,
  b = model1$theta,
  se = model1$se,
  t = model1$theta / model1$se,
  p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(model1$theta / model1$se))
)
```

The first model converges at 0.12, which is lower than the 0.25 threshold and all convergence
t-ratios are smaller than 0.1, with the maximum convergence t-ratio of -0.09.

**Table 2:** *Results of Model 1*

```{r}
pander::pander(results_m1)
```

The first model is used to look at whether reciprocated ties are more likely to occur among students

## Model 1: Homogeneity in reciprocated ties

```{r, include= FALSE}
#goodness of fit practicalities
GeodesicDistribution <- function(i, data, sims, period, groupName, varName, levls = c(1:5, Inf), cumulative = TRUE,
    ...) {
    x <- networkExtraction(i, data, sims, period, groupName, varName)
    require(network)
    require(sna)
    a <- sna::geodist(symmetrize(x))$gdist
    if (cumulative) {
        gdi <- sapply(levls, function(i) {
            sum(a <= i)
        })
    } else {
        gdi <- sapply(levls, function(i) {
            sum(a == i)
        })
    }
    names(gdi) <- as.character(levls)
    gdi
}

# The following function is taken from the help page for sienaTest

testall <- function(ans) {
    for (i in which(ans$test)) {
        sct <- score.Test(ans, i)
        cat(ans$requestedEffects$effectName[i], "\n")
        print(sct)
    }
    invisible(score.Test(ans))
}
```

```{r}

```


## Model 2: Homogeneity in reciprocated ties with control variables

```{r}
myeff2 <- includeEffects(myeff1.3, egoX, altX, sameX, sameXRecip, interaction1 = "gender_ccv")
myeff2 <- includeEffects(myeff1.3, egoX, altX, sameX, sameXRecip, interaction1 = "ethnicity_ccv")
myeff2
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
model2 <- siena07(myAlgorithm, data = mydata, effects = myeff2, thetaBound = 10000, returnDeps = T)
model2
#saveRDS(model2, "model2.rds")
```

## Model 3: Reciprocity and social satisfaction

```{r}
myeff3 <- includeEffects(myeff2, name = "behMLC", recipDeg, avRecAlt, interaction1 = "netMLC")
myeff3
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
model3 <- siena07(myAlgorithm, data = mydata, effects = myeff3, thetaBound = 10000, returnDeps = T)
model3
#saveRDS(model3, "model3.rds")
```

## Model 4: Reciprocity between same covariates and social satisfaction

```{r}
myeff4 <- set_effect(myeff3, list(avRecAltSameX, avSameXRecAlt), depvar = "behMLC", covar1 = "parent_edu_ccv", covar2 = "netMLC")
myeff4
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
model4 <- siena07(myAlgorithm, data = mydata, effects = myeff4, thetaBound = 10000, returnDeps = T)
model4
#saveRDS(model4, "model4.rds")
```
